title: Power Rankings: Cavs on top, Nets no longer last
heading: 2009-10 Power Rankings: Week 22
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: The Cavs actually had 61 wins at this same point last season, but we're still standing by what was said in this cyberspace precisely one Monday ago: This season's Cavs will be proceeding to postseason with more momentum.

rankings.summaryHtml: This was just insanity: Redick takes Carter's place after 95 seconds in a home W over Denver and rings up 23 points, eight assists and seven boards. Vinsanity hasn't hit those totals in the same game all season.

rankings.summaryHtml: Instead of the Bobs' usual nightmare schedule in April, this is reasonable: Six of their final 10 games are at home and the four road dates (Chicago, New Orleans, Houston and New Jersey) aren't exactly unwinnable.

rankings.summaryHtml: Comeback Coach of the Year? The award still doesn't exist, but Del Negro's Bulls are in the midst of another resurrection -- four wins out of five after a 10-game losing skid -- that has No. 8 seed Toronto totally freaked out.

rankings.summaryHtml: At 6½ games out of the final playoff spot in the West with nine to play, all the Griz can do now is try to secure a winning season by scraping out four more W's from a schedule offering just two more sub-.500 opponents.
